agents.name: Tepotinib
agents.explanation: Tepotinib inhibits the MET receptor. A MET exon 14 skipping change can keep this growth signal active; blocking it can slow or shrink selected lung cancers.
agents.watch: Report new cough or breathlessness, swelling, severe bowel symptoms, jaundice, palpitations or fainting promptly.
risks: Lung inflammation, which can be serious or fatal
Liver test changes and possible liver injury

sections.title: Before starting
sections.text: Confirm the MET result, previous treatment, prescription, first review and contact number.

sections.title: Taking your tablets
sections.text: Take at the same time each day with food and swallow whole. If a dose is missed, take it when remembered on the same day unless the next dose is due within 8 hours; then skip it. Do not double a dose. Ask your pharmacist if the timing is uncertain or if you vomit; do not take a replacement without advice. If swallowing is difficult, ask about the approved water-dispersion method.

sections.title: Supplies and reviews
sections.text: Arrange repeat prescriptions before tablets run out. Keep blood-test and review appointments. The tablet regimen itself needs no infusion line or pump.

sections.title: If treatment is held
sections.text: Ask why, what must recover, when review is due and who will authorise restarting. Do not change between one and two tablets yourself.

sections.title: At a change or stop
sections.text: Agree scans, symptom follow-up and the medicine plan. Continue the contraception and breastfeeding precautions for at least one week after the final dose.

evidence.heading: Evidence for this treatment
evidence.summary: VISION found that tepotinib could shrink some advanced MET exon 14 skipping lung cancers, including cancers previously treated with other medicines. It was a single-arm study, so it does not show how much longer people live compared with another treatment. Study results describe groups and cannot predict your own outcome.
evidence.limitations: Single-arm evidence does not establish comparative survival benefit; first-line trial patients are outside this NCCP indication.

patient.teachback: Can you explain why the MET result and previous treatment matter, how you take the tablets with food, what to do if a dose is missed, and which symptoms mean you should call today?
patient.consent_support: Discuss the advanced-disease treatment aim, possible benefit and uncertainty, alternatives including not proceeding, daily tablets with food, swelling and bowel effects, serious lung/liver/heart risks, monitoring, pregnancy and fertility, and the right to reconsider.

support.title: Swelling and weight changes
support.text: Report swelling early and discuss changes in weight, movement or breathing. The team will assess the cause and agree treatment; do not start a water tablet or change tepotinib yourself.

support.title: Diarrhoea and fluids
support.text: Agree a diarrhoea treatment plan before starting. Begin the prescribed anti-diarrhoeal medicine at the first loose stool as instructed, and maintain fluids if able. Persistent diarrhoea, weakness or reduced urine needs prompt advice.

support.title: Nausea medicines
support.text: Tepotinib has minimal-to-low oral emetic risk. Agree an as-needed anti-sickness plan with the team, including medicine-interaction and heart-rhythm checks; no routine infusion premedication is specified.

support.title: Medicine review
support.text: Ask the pharmacist to check all prescribed medicines, non-prescription medicines and supplements before changes. Tepotinib can affect medicines including dabigatran, digoxin, rosuvastatin and metformin. Supportive medicines may also affect heart rhythm; individual advice is needed.

support.title: Pregnancy, fertility and breastfeeding
support.text: Avoid pregnancy during treatment. Effective contraception is needed during treatment and for at least one week after the last dose; women using hormonal contraception should also use a barrier method. Men with a partner who could become pregnant should use barrier contraception for the same period. Do not breastfeed during treatment or for at least one week afterwards. Human fertility effects are not known; discuss fertility before starting.

chapters.title: What studies tell us
chapters.intro: VISION found that tepotinib could shrink some advanced MET exon 14 skipping lung cancers, including cancers previously treated with other medicines. It was a single-arm study, so it does not show how much longer people live compared with another treatment. Study results describe groups and cannot predict your own outcome.

items.text: Ask how closely the trial population matches your situation and discuss alternatives and remaining uncertainties.

chapters.intro: The team authorises continuation, a pause, restart or stopping.

items.text: Agree who will review test results and confirm the dose. A source reduction to 225 mg is a clinician decision, not an instruction to halve tablets yourself.

questions.q: Is this a fixed course of chemotherapy?
questions.a: No. These targeted tablets are taken daily without a planned rest week, while they are helping and your team considers treatment appropriate.

questions.q: Why does a trial mention 500 mg?
questions.a: The VISION trial’s 500 mg salt dose corresponds to 450 mg active tepotinib. The prescribed tablets contain 225 mg active tepotinib each; follow your own prescription.

questions.q: What if I forget or vomit a dose?
questions.a: Take a forgotten dose when remembered on the same day unless the next dose is due within 8 hours; then skip it. Never double up. Ask your pharmacist about vomiting or uncertain timing before taking any replacement.

questions.q: Why might my creatinine test change?
questions.a: Tepotinib can change how creatinine is handled by the kidneys, but real kidney problems can also occur. The team must assess the change; neither explanation should be assumed.

questions.q: Can I change the dose when I feel better?
questions.a: Only your team can authorise restarting or changing the dose after side effects. Feeling better does not establish that blood tests or other checks have recovered.

clinical.component_rationale: Tepotinib inhibits MET signalling in METex14-skipping NSCLC. This is monotherapy after immunotherapy and/or platinum chemotherapy; no cytotoxic component or fixed number of cycles is added.
key_points: NCCP 00823a covers tepotinib on its own for adults with advanced non-small cell lung cancer carrying a confirmed MET exon 14 skipping change, after immunotherapy and/or platinum chemotherapy. It is not a first-line or adjuvant treatment guide.
Usual starting dose 450 mg active tepotinib (two 225 mg tablets) daily with food; VISION 500 mg is the salt dose, corresponding to 450 mg active moiety.
Keep suspected and confirmed ILD distinct at every grade.
Retain bilirubin and cholestasis/haemolysis qualifiers for liver discontinuation and the seven-day recovery-to-baseline distinction.
Renal impairment below CrCl 30 mL/min / dialysis requires explicit reconciliation of NCCP and current SmPC.
Other grade ≥3 adverse reactions use the 225 mg pathway or a considered interruption no longer than 21 days; no automatic repeat halving or re-escalation.

disease_and_biomarker_context: NCCP 00823a: adults with advanced NSCLC, validated MET exon 14 skipping alteration, after immunotherapy and/or platinum chemotherapy.
No activating EGFR mutation or ALK rearrangement; NCCP ECOG 0–2. VISION largely enrolled ECOG 0–1, limiting direct extrapolation to ECOG 2.
patient_selection.treatment_intent: Advanced disease control after immunotherapy and/or platinum chemotherapy.
eligibility_orientation: Assess renal/hepatic function, respiratory history, oedema, nutrition and functional status.
Child–Pugh C is not recommended. CrCl <30 / dialysis requires resolving the source discrepancy before a dose decision.
NCCP 00823a: advanced METex14 NSCLC after immunotherapy and/or platinum chemotherapy.
Validated MET exon 14 skipping alteration; no activating EGFR mutation or ALK rearrangement.
important_cautions: NCCP exclusions: hypersensitivity, active CNS metastases, pregnancy or breastfeeding.
ILD and QTc risk are explicit cautions; clinically stable CNS disease must not be equated with active CNS disease.
Discuss single-arm efficacy evidence and alternatives; no comparative survival benefit is established.
Agree monitoring, medicine supply, adherence, side-effect support and contact plan.

support_summary: Minimal-to-low oral emetic risk; individual as-needed antiemetics under local policy, no specified routine premedication. NCCP lists loperamide 4 mg at first loose stool then 2 mg after each loose stool (maximum 16 mg/day), or local policy; check the individual prescription and escalation plan. Review interactions and QT risk when selecting supportive medicines.

Ask the pharmacist to check all prescribed medicines, non-prescription medicines and supplements before changes. Tepotinib can affect medicines including dabigatran, digoxin, rosuvastatin and metformin. Supportive medicines may also affect heart rhythm; individual advice is needed.

Avoid pregnancy during treatment. Effective contraception is needed during treatment and for at least one week after the last dose; women using hormonal contraception should also use a barrier method. Men with a partner who could become pregnant should use barrier contraception for the same period. Do not breastfeed during treatment or for at least one week afterwards. baseline: Confirm the MET result, previous treatment, dose, other medicines and emergency contact. Check blood count, electrolytes, kidney and liver function; ECG if clinically indicated. Discuss pregnancy, contraception and breastfeeding, and perform a pregnancy test when applicable.
before_each_cycle: No chemotherapy cycle is defined. At scheduled reviews check FBC, electrolytes, renal/liver profile, symptoms, weight/oedema, adherence and medicines.
ongoing: Repeat blood count, electrolytes, kidney and liver tests at the team’s agreed reviews. ECG is used when clinically indicated. Report new lung symptoms, swelling, diarrhoea or vomiting between visits. A rise in creatinine needs assessment because the medicine can change the test result without necessarily damaging the kidneys. Scans follow the Consultant’s plan.
Liver enzymes and bilirubin before starting and thereafter as clinically indicated; no invented monthly or two-weekly cadence.
Pregnancy testing during treatment if clinically indicated.
administration: Take at the same time each day with food and swallow whole. If a dose is missed, take it when remembered on the same day unless the next dose is due within 8 hours; then skip it. Do not double a dose. Ask your pharmacist if the timing is uncertain or if you vomit; do not take a replacement without advice. If swallowing is difficult, ask about the approved water-dispersion method.
Usual dose 450 mg active tepotinib daily. Source reduction level 225 mg daily; all modifications discussed with Consultant.

For inability to swallow: SmPC permits dispersion in 30 mL non-carbonated water without crushing, administration within one hour, and a 30 mL rinse; tube administration has separate instructions and requires pharmacy supervision.
access: Oral medicine; no infusion access or ambulatory pump is intrinsic to this regimen. Tests, scans and clinical reviews still require a planned service.
Confirm reliable medicine supply, test ownership and a 24-hour oncology contact.

drug_mechanisms.tepotinib: Reversible ATP-competitive MET tyrosine kinase inhibitor; suppresses MET phosphorylation and downstream PI3K/Akt and MAPK/ERK signalling in tumours with activating MET alterations.

rationale.summary: Biomarker-directed monotherapy for advanced METex14-skipping NSCLC after prior immunotherapy and/or platinum chemotherapy, supported by the nonrandomised VISION cohorts.
benefit_and_uncertainty: VISION found that tepotinib could shrink some advanced MET exon 14 skipping lung cancers, including cancers previously treated with other medicines. It was a single-arm study, so it does not show how much longer people live compared with another treatment. Study results describe groups and cannot predict your own outcome.
limitations: No randomised comparator in VISION; objective response and duration of response do not prove an overall-survival advantage.
Do not substitute treatment-naive, Asian-only or long-responder selected-subset outcomes for the entire previously treated population.
Current NCCP operational eligibility and EU indication take precedence over broader trial recruitment.
factors: Validated MET alteration, previous treatment, performance status, organ function, CNS status and patient priorities.
Respiratory history, oedema, QT risk, medicine interactions and ability to take daily tablets.
alternatives: Discuss current MDT-approved systemic options, clinical trials and supportive care, including not proceeding.

evidence.trial: VISION phase 2, cohorts A and C
evidence.population: Advanced/metastatic METex14-skipping NSCLC; previously treated subgroup n=149 within combined cohorts n=313. Trial ECOG 0–1; NCCP eligibility is 0–2.
evidence.comparison: Single-arm, nonrandomised study; no concurrent control group.
evidence.applicability: VISION found that tepotinib could shrink some advanced MET exon 14 skipping lung cancers, including cancers previously treated with other medicines. It was a single-arm study, so it does not show how much longer people live compared with another treatment. Study results describe groups and cannot predict your own outcome.

endpoints.metric: Previously treated subgroup: confirmed objective response by independent review
endpoints.interpretation: 95% CI 36.8–53.3%; response by RECIST 1.1 in the previously treated population. Do not use the treatment-naive response rate for NCCP 00823a.
endpoints.analysis_status: Peer-reviewed long-term follow-up, corroborated in EMA SmPC Table 3

endpoints.metric: Previously treated subgroup: median duration of response
endpoints.interpretation: 95% CI 9.5–18.5 months; applies to responders, not all treated patients, and is not median survival.
endpoints.time_origin: First documented objective response to progression or death
endpoints.analysis_status: Peer-reviewed long-term follow-up, corroborated in EMA SmPC Table 3

limitations: No randomised comparator or established comparative overall-survival advantage; no hazard ratio is assigned.

The 2025 ≥3-year follow-up abstract (cutoff 20 May 2024) retains 45.0% response in the previously treated group. It is a conference abstract, separately labelled rather than presented as a new full-paper survival claim.
The 2026 ASCO abstract selects long responders with duration >36 months. This outcome-selected subgroup cannot estimate the probability of durable benefit for a new patient.
NCCP/EU setting requires previous immunotherapy and/or platinum chemotherapy; first-line trial data do not expand the indication. Active CNS metastases remain an NCCP exclusion.
Trial dose 500 mg tepotinib hydrochloride hydrate corresponds to 450 mg active tepotinib. Trial results are not individual prognoses.
evidence.harms: Swelling/fluid retention, nausea, diarrhoea and laboratory changes are important burdens. ILD can be fatal; hepatic and QT risks need distinct assessment. Adverse-event percentages from different attribution methods are not compared.
